- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid overshoot.
- If recent history shows sharp upward moves followed by a drop, model tends to overcorrect — dampen forecast peak and allow gradual decline.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is flat or rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid false optimism.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in early days of forecast horizon, adjust future values downward by 1–2% per day to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3–0.6), forecast should be more conservative — avoid steep upward trends unless sentiment is consistently bullish.
- For 30-day forecasts, if first 3–5 days show large divergence (e.g., >5% error), reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for lag and volatility.
- When sentiment peaks early and price spikes, model often overreacts — cap forecast at 1–2% above peak sentiment level to avoid overcorrection.
